assumptions: One canonical positive-potential scalar provides early and late energy; smooth rolling depletion is approximated by successive constant-slope regimes.
EDE normalization fixes illustrative lambda_early^2=40; residual fraction target is order 1%; lambda_late^2=0.25 is a benchmark, not a fit.
Source sign/convention corrections must precede implementation; background trajectory does not close the observational/perturbation test.
Finite sum V=sum V_i exp(-lambda_i phi) has V_i>0 and constant slopes; phi is expressed in reduced-Planck units.
The history under consideration rolls monotonically toward increasing phi. Negative coefficients, direction changes and other potentials are excluded from this identity.
Baryon-free matter-scaling fixed-point F, constant beta, physical nonnegative x/y/energy fractions and the source KG/continuity convention.
3/(2lambda^2) and 3/8 are large-lambda approximations; baryon-inclusive generality remains unresolved because of Appendix signs/nonuniformity.
